answer.rationale: The 18% cost cut is the binding constraint; negotiate_terms is the only direction that attacks cost without adding delivery risk in the 14-day window. Memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments with the incumbent already unlocked volume pricing and cut unit cost without narrowing scope — extending that logic under the new budget mandate should yield further concessions. Memory_c4 shows benchmarking at renewal moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms. Memory_c1 confirms the incumbent has maintained stable integration with no interruption. Verifying memory_c6 and memory_c2 before committing ensures the incumbent's true concession history and the low-cost vendor's actual performance are on record. switch_primary_vendor is rejected: the 14-day window is too tight for onboarding a new primary, and the assembly line is at 94% with no buffer — any integration hiccup breaches delivery commitments. add_second_source is deferred: it does not reduce cost this cycle and only mitigates risk. defer_decision is rejected: the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, and deferring past expiry would strand the supply line.
